Subject: Redwood eval - cost/TCO and next tests

Thanks again for the chat today — great to learn more about Nimbus's ingestion volume and latency targets. Per our call, I wanted to capture the follow-ups and propose a short test plan so we can give you apples-to-apples numbers vs the hyperscaler endpoints you're evaluating.

Recap / asks from the discovery:
- Workload: real-time document summarization + reranking for 100k monthly active users; ~6k concurrent requests peak; typical request length ~600 tokens input with 200 token outputs.
- Current baseline: experimenting with OpenAI + batching at the app layer; notable variance in latency when traffic spikes.
- Security: SOC2 + VPC peering required for production.

Next steps we propose (short and actionable):
1) Run a 48-hour bench vs 1M token equivalent using your sample prompt set (we'll provide instructions).
2) Measure: p50/p95 latency, cost per 1M tokens, and cache hit rates with a 7-day prefix cache window.
3) Run two configs on Redwood: a) optimized-batch (aggressive batching, 128 token bucket) and b) low-latency (smaller batch, KV cache warm).

We can provide the benchmark harness and a TCO model so you can simulate monthly spend with different cache hit and batching assumptions. I've attached a starter TCO workbook and the benchmark instructions. Marcus will follow up with estimated unit economics (per-1M tokens) for the configs we discussed.

Proposed schedule: we can kick off the bench as early as Monday if you can share the prompts and a service account for the Drive link in the instructions.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Redwood eval - cost/TCO and next tests

Hey Priya — quick answers and high-level unit economics to help set expectations before you run the bench.

1) Token accounting: our public pricing and the model runs we quote count both input + output tokens (total tokens). We'll show numbers per-1M total tokens.

2) Batching interplay: Redwood's runtime does continuous batching at the inference layer. If you also micro-batch at the client, we'll observe larger batched sizes; the platform supports an inbound max_batch_size and a batch_timeout to tune. For low-latency config we'll set max_batch_size=8, batch_timeout=20ms; for optimized-batch config we use max_batch_size=64, batch_timeout=80ms.

3) Ballpark unit economics (per-1M total tokens) — these are estimates for the model family we discussed (open Llama-style baseline) on a redwood-hosted Dedicated instance:
- Low-latency config: $14.50 per 1M tokens (higher because of smaller batches & priority capacity)
- Optimized-batch config: $5.90 per 1M tokens (bigger batches, cache savings)

Notes on assumptions:
- Cache hit rate impact: each 10% increase in prefix-KV cache hit rate reduces per-1M cost by ~7% in the optimized profile (due to fewer compute tokens).
- We included networking and host amortization in the Dedicated pricing; hosted API pricing for the same model family typically runs ~20-30% higher (no reserved capacity).

I attached the detailed TCO workbook (baseline tabs) and a short benchmark checklist. Pull figures into the workbook after your run and we can iterate on the model/quantization tradeoffs.

If you want, we can also run a short 4-hour comparative bench vs OpenAI (their API) and Bedrock in your account to show delta in p95 and cost. That usually helps procurement.

—Marcus Lin
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
